question.text: Scenario: Capital Edge Research Pvt Ltd is a newly registered research entity planning to set up operations. The founder, Nikhil Shah, is designing the firm's compliance framework. He needs to address: (1) How to structure analyst compensation without creating IB conflicts. (2) What disclosures to include in every research report. (3) How to handle situations where the firm also provides IB advisory services. (4) What trading restrictions to impose on analysts and their associates. (5) How to maintain a website as per SEBI requirements. The firm plans to cover 50 companies across 5 sectors, employ 8 full-time analysts and 3 part-time analysts, and offer both subscription-based research and fee-based advisory services to accredited investors. Question 5 of 5: Capital Edge's website must contain:

answer.text: Only the firm's logo and office address

A functional website with details specified by SEBI, including registered name/logo/registration/address/contact and required disclaimer (where applicable), Investor Charter, complaint disclosures and complaints data, and complaint/SCORES access
Only a contact form for inquiries
Only links to published research reports

explanation.text: The Logic: A research analyst must maintain a functional website containing details specified by SEBI. The Investor Charter must be disclosed on the website and mobile app, complaints must be disclosed/linked, and complaints data must be published in the prescribed website/mobile-app format with access to the SEBI SCORES complaint system. The Trap: Business activity, disciplinary history, terms of service, and associate details are framed as client/material disclosures rather than the website-specific rule itself. Note: The website rule (functional website + SEBI-specified content + Investor Charter + complaints disclosure/data + SCORES access) is distinct from the broader client/material disclosure list.
